_: The five findings of the red (Screening) hero, in the EXACT keys lot S1 declared (message of the night of 5 to 6). Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-screening/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; S1 refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches that seal, and this file names each figure's cell in `source` beside it: {table, palier, seuil, mesure} reads releve[table].tables[palier][seuil][mesure] ({succes, n, taux, bas, haut}); {table, compte} reads releve[table][compte]. `source` is provenance for reviewers and future guards; builders may ignore it. Intervals in legends are Wilson 95% from the same cells, en dash, never an em dash. The rule behind finding 03 is the tool's own default (optimise: Wilson lower bound of recall >= 0.90, then the fewest false alerts), the same rule the live instrument applies: one rule on the whole site, chosen, not measured, and said on the fiche. `annotations` are fractions of the rendered tower box (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text), placed by the chef on the rendered states.

findings.titre: Exact matching raises no false alert and misses most confirmed matches.
findings.phrase: Exact matching, after normalisation, raises no false alert on the 60 written non-match pairs, and finds 21.7% of the confirmed matches.
findings.leg_a: recall 21.7% on 60 written match pairs, interval [13–34], at any threshold
findings.leg_b: false alerts 0% on 60 written non-match pairs, interval [0–6]

findings.titre: The loosest threshold finds every match and alerts on 85% of non-matches.
findings.phrase: At the loosest threshold the matcher finds every confirmed match on the 60 pairs, and alerts on 85% of the non-match pairs; each false alert is analyst time.
findings.leg_a: recall 100% at the loosest threshold, interval [94–100], 60 match pairs
findings.leg_b: false alerts 85% at the same threshold, interval [74–92], 60 non-match pairs

findings.titre: The best trade-off keeps 98.3% recall at 76.7% false alerts.
findings.phrase: The tool keeps the recall floor at 90%, then reads the cost. Across every model tier and threshold, the embedding included, the best trade-off is jaro-winkler at 0.56: recall 98.3%, and still 76.7% false alerts.
findings.leg_a: recall 98.3% at jaro‑winkler 0.56, interval [91–100], 60 match pairs
findings.leg_b: false alerts 76.7% at the same cell, interval [65–86]

findings.titre: Fabricated variants score 17.2% false alerts against 76.7% on written pairs.
findings.phrase: The same cell reads 76.7% false alerts on the 60 written pairs and 17.2% on the 360 fabricated variants. The fabricated set is easier, so it is measured on its own and never merged into the headline rate.
findings.leg_a: false alerts 76.7% at the best cell on 60 written pairs, interval [65–86]
findings.leg_b: false alerts 17.2% at the same cell on 360 fabricated variants, interval [14–21]

findings.titre: The public record holds 60 written pairs and 360 fabricated variants.
findings.phrase: Every pair behind these findings is in the public record: 60 written and declared, 360 fabricated and labelled. One command reruns the full sweep on your own alert history at your desk.
findings.leg_a: written match and non-match pairs behind the measured rates, declared by typology
findings.leg_b: fabricated variants behind the separate rates, labelled and measured apart
annotations: written pairs behind the measured rates
